summary: Phase 7 targeted testing of Monitoring IB & Quick Check PHP+MariaDB app. 16/17 backend pytest cases pass; 1 real backend bug found (double-cancel accepted). All 9 sidebar pages navigate without console errors. Critical UI flows verified: login, personnel search/filter/import-preview, device approve+revoke, IB create+detail+cancel, quick-check with duration, geofence modal map picker, reports table+CSV download, settings (pw form, users, audit), logout, wrong-password error. Admin password restored to admin123.

critical.issue: Double-cancel is silently accepted (returns 200). Requirement per Phase 7 spec: 'cancelled session cannot be cancelled twice'. Root cause: MonitoringController::cancel calls MonitoringSession::cancel which does UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ('SCHEDULED','ACTIVE') so a no-op on already-CANCELLED — but the controller does not check the current status or the affected rowCount before returning success. Fix: in cancel controller, check $session['status'] === 'CANCELLED' and Response::error('Monitoring sudah dibatalkan.', 409), OR check PDO rowCount() after UPDATE.

integration_issues.issue: Typing '320002' in [data-testid=history-search] did not surface visible autocomplete suggestions and the 'Tampilkan' button remained hidden — probably requires a specific suggest element the user must click before the load button appears. Should be reviewed for discoverability (may just be styling of dropdown), but no JS errors were thrown.

action_items: Fix POST /api/monitoring/{id}/cancel to reject a second cancel with 409/422 (see RCA).
critical_code_review_comments: MonitoringController::cancel does not enforce idempotency/rejection for already-CANCELLED sessions — this is the direct source of the double-cancel bug. It also does not consult rowCount() from the UPDATE, so callers cannot tell if cancel really occurred.
MonitoringSession::cancel uses a WHERE guard on status but silently succeeds when 0 rows are affected; consider returning the affected row count and having the controller act on it.

AuthController::changePassword expects field name 'current_password' — the field is exposed to admins via UI; consistent naming is fine but ensure API docs / mobile / any other client use the same key.

rca of the issue: Double-cancel bug: (1) Reproduce — create IB via POST /api/monitoring/ib, POST /api/monitoring/{id}/cancel twice; both return 200 success. (2) Root cause — MonitoringController::cancel at /app/project/backend/controllers/MonitoringController.php:149 blindly returns Response::success after calling MonitoringSession::cancel(). The model performs 'UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ("SCHEDULED","ACTIVE")' which is a no-op on an already CANCELLED row, but no check on prior status or PDOStatement->rowCount() is performed. (3) Mitigation — insert before MonitoringSession::cancel: if ($session['status'] === 'CANCELLED') Response::error('Monitoring sudah dibatalkan.', 409); (Or check rowCount from cancel() and error out on 0.)
